---
title: "Backends"
---

phibble separates what a pipeline does from where it runs. Every verb is part
of the `Phibble\Contracts\Table` interface, and three classes implement it:

| Backend | Class | Runs | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| In memory | `Phibble\DataFrame` | PHP arrays | Small and medium data, closures, anything |
| SQL | `Phibble\Sql\SqlTable` | SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL | Data that lives in a database |
| Polars | `Phibble\Polars\PolarsTable` | Polars, through the php_polars extension | Large data in memory |

All three classes are part of phibble. `PolarsTable` uses the php_polars
extension, which [phpolars](https://github.com/phpstats/phpolars) provides.

Code written against `Table`, including phplyr's verbs, runs on any of them. A
backend that cannot run a step exactly, such as a PHP closure or a function
with no exact translation, hands that step to `DataFrame` and continues. The
values then match `DataFrame` with these exceptions:

- A database cannot represent some of R's values, such as `NaN` in MySQL. The
  [SQL tables](sql.qmd#known-differences) page lists these cases.
- Rows from a SQL join, and from a table without `arrange()`, come back in the
  order the database returns them.
- Floating-point results can differ in the last digits. The SQL and Polars
  tests compare floats rounded to nine decimal places.

The [Table contract](contract.qmd) page states the rules each backend follows.

## Choosing and switching

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use function Phibble\{tbl, polars};
use function Phibble\Expr\{col, mean, n};

$df = DataFrame::fromCsv('sales.csv');
$sql = tbl($pdo, 'sales');
$fast = polars($df);

$summary = fn ($t) => $t
    ->filter(col('units')->gt(0))
    ->groupBy(['store'])
    ->summarize(['n' => n(), 'avg' => mean(col('price'))]);

$summary($df);
$summary($sql)->collect();
$summary($fast)->collect();
```

`$df` holds the data in memory, `$sql` reads it from the database, and
`$fast` holds it in Polars. On `$sql`, the summary runs as one SQL query.
All three classes have `summarize()` as an alias of the `Table` method
`summarise()`. Code that accepts any `Table` implementation should call
`summarise()`, since the interface declares only that name.

`collect()` turns any table into a `DataFrame`. `PolarsTable::fromTable()` and
`polars()` move a table into Polars; `tbl()` opens a database table or query.

## The Polars backend

phibble's `Phibble\Polars\PolarsTable` needs the php_polars extension, which
phpolars builds. phibble does not require it: `composer.json` lists it as a
suggestion, and the class is only loaded when used. Expressions, joins (including `join_by` comparisons and rolling joins),
pivots, and the lubridate and stringr functions run natively in Polars. Steps
it cannot run, such as PHP closures and `str_to_title()`, run in `DataFrame`.
`PolarsTable::$fallbacks` counts those steps. Set `PolarsTable::$strict = true`
to throw `PolarsFallback` instead. The message names the verb and the reason.

A time column is a Polars duration in microseconds, which, like an hms, can
be negative or longer than a day. A Polars `Time` column reads as a time.
Comparisons of times, `is_na()`, `min()`, `max()`, `first()`, and `last()` run
in Polars, and other functions of a time run in a `DataFrame`.

Two kinds of list-column stay in `DataFrame`. Polars stores named arrays as
structs, which have every key in every row, so `fromTable()` throws when a
list-column holds named arrays with different keys. A list-column of
`DataFrame`s cannot be stored in Polars either.

The Polars test suite runs phibble's dplyr, tidyr, lubridate, and stringr
reference cases on `PolarsTable` and skips when the extension is not loaded.
